\section{Even unimodular lattices}
A lattice $L \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ is \emph{even} if $x \cdot x \in 2\mathbb{Z}$ for all $x \in L$,
and \emph{unimodular} if $\det L = \pm 1$.
\begin{theorem}
An even unimodular positive definite lattice of rank $n$ exists if and only if $8 \mid n$.
\end{theorem}
\[ \theta_{E_8}(q) = 1 + 240 \sum_{n \geq 1} \sigma_3(n) q^n. \]
\newpage
\section{Discriminant forms}
For an even lattice $L$ the discriminant group is $A_L = L^\vee / L$ with the form
$q_L(x) = x \cdot x \bmod 2\mathbb{Z}$.
